# 1. Importing Data from Statistical Packages

The `haven` package imports data from SPSS, Stata, and SAS files.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(haven)

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Create sample data for testing
survey <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  age = c(25, 30, 35, 40, 45),
  score = c(70, 85, 90, 60, 75)
)

# Save data in different formats
write_sav(survey, "data/survey.sav")
write_dta(survey, "data/survey.dta")
write_xpt(survey, "data/survey.xpt")
```

## Import the files

```{r}
spss_data <- read_sav("data/survey.sav")
stata_data <- read_dta("data/survey.dta")
sas_data <- read_xpt("data/survey.xpt")

head(spss_data)
head(stata_data)
head(sas_data)
```

## Check the imported data

```{r}
dim(spss_data)
dim(stata_data)
dim(sas_data)
```

Each dataset should contain 5 rows and 3 columns.

# 2. Importing Data from a Database

The `DBI` package provides an interface for connecting R to databases. The `RSQLite` package allows R to work with SQLite databases.

```{r database-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)

# Connect to an SQLite database
con <- dbConnect(
  SQLite(),
  "data/company.sqlite"
)

# Create a sample table
employees <- data.frame(
  name = c("Aime", "Fidele", "Iradukunda", "Arstide"),
  dept = c("IT", "HR", "IT", "Finance"),
  salary = c(1200, 800, 1500, 1000)
)

dbWriteTable(con, "employees", employees, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Read data from the database

```{r}
# Import the complete table
employee_data <- dbReadTable(con, "employees")
print(employee_data)

# Import selected records using SQL
it_employees <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT * FROM employees WHERE dept = 'IT'"
)

print(it_employees)

# Close the connection
dbDisconnect(con)
```

# 3. Conclusion

The `haven` package imports SPSS, Stata, and SAS files. The `DBI` and `RSQLite` packages connect R to SQLite databases and retrieve data using R functions and SQL queries.
